function.mechanism: Used as an antimicrobial preservative; paraben-class compounds are associated with membrane-disruptive antimicrobial effects (mechanistic inference from paraben literature).
common_food_categories: foods with reported paraben occurrence in monitoring studies (e.g., vegetables, condiments, bakery products)

adi.basis: Full group ADI for the sum of methyl and ethyl p-hydroxybenzoic acid esters and their sodium salts.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA established/maintained a group ADI for methyl+ethyl parabens and EU later kept E214 with tightened use limits.

adi.basis: Group ADI as the sum of the ethyl and methyl esters of p-hydroxybenzoic acid.

concerns.summary: Mouse studies reported impaired implantation/decidualization and embryo developmental toxicity at high oral/in vitro exposure levels of ethylparaben.
Recent dietary/exposure literature indicates possible cumulative paraben exposure concerns in some settings outside tightly regulated markets.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported no hormonal/reproductive effects for methyl/ethyl parabens in the reviewed juvenile-rat data and set group ADI 0-10 mg/kg bw/day.
JECFA maintains ADI 0-10 mg/kg bw for methyl+ethyl parabens.

populations: high consumers of multiple paraben-containing processed foods
adi_exceedance.notes: Evidence for exceedance is scenario-dependent and strongest in cumulative-exposure analyses; Taiwan probabilistic assessment reported paraben hazard indices below 1.

risk_assessment.rationale: E214 has established EFSA/JECFA ADIs and remains regulated (not banned), but high-dose animal reproductive/developmental signals and cumulative exposure concerns justify caution.
key_factors: EFSA/JECFA group ADI of 0-10 mg/kg bw/day
EU retains E214 with tighter maximum levels rather than withdrawal
No IARC listing found for ethylparaben
Animal mechanistic concern studies at high exposures
Cumulative exposure may exceed ADI in some non-EU/high-intake scenarios
